statement_record.book: (a) If K : M → C has a right Kan extension R along itself, with φ : Nat(S,R) ≅ Nat(SK,K), then ⟨R, η, μ⟩ with η = φ⁻¹(id_K), μ = φ⁻¹(ε·Rε) is a monad on C — the codensity monad of K. (b) K is codense iff η is an isomorphism. (c) If G : A → X has a left adjoint F (unit η:1→GF, counit ε:FG→Id), its codensity monad exists and equals ⟨GF, η, GεF⟩, the monad of the adjunction.
statement_record.intree: Adjunction_Induced_Monad : @Monad D (U ◯ F) with ret x = η x (adjunction unit) and join x = fmap[U] (ε (F x)) (adjunction counit) — i.e. ⟨GF, η, GεF⟩. This is precisely part (c)'s asserted RHS, present verbatim; but it is built from the adjunction directly, NOT as a codensity monad / Kan extension.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only part (c)'s target monad exists, and it is not identified as a codensity monad.
